text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in a statement on Friday that he had signed documents that would change France's takeover rules and extend the period for hostile bids.
He said that by extending the period, shareholders would have 25 trading days before the closing of a bid to make up their mind instead of the 10 to 13 days currently.

He added that investors would now have to declare their intention when they obtain a 10 percent stake in a company. Currently this limit is 20 percent. A new declaration of intent will have to be made when the 20 percent level is reached.
Under the new takeover rules, drawn up by the new financial markets body CMF, a bid cannot be started before an information notice has been published by the bidder.
The closing date of the bid will be 25 trading days after the publication of a defence document by the company which is subject to the bid.
But to prevent a company from delaying the process by waiting with the publication of a defence document, a limit on the total lenght of a bid period has been put at 35 trading days.
The Finance Ministry said that the rules made the market more transparent and were in line with rules on international markets.
It added that the existing levels at which an investors had to notify share market watchdog COB about stakes remained at five, 10, 20, 33.33, 50 and 66.66 percent of the share capital.
This notification has to be made within five trading days.
The declaration of intent, at 10 and 20 percent, concerns the 12 months after the level has been reached.

Non-respect of the rules can lead to a two-year suspension by the COB of the company's voting rights in shareholders meetings for the number of shares which exceeds the level, as well as by administrative sanctions that could go to 10 million francs.
